City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
November 5, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on November 5, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on October 31, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley
INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update from and provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Oral Histories Project Presentation
The City Council received the presentation from Director of Library Services Stephanie Tanton and Community Services Commissioner Robert Breton.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern with the Mayor’s acceptance of a campaign donation from Sentinel Development, owners of Kaleidoscope, and that candidate Wendy Bucknum held a fundraising event at Kaleidoscope. Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that a group of volunteers put a website together, missionviejobusiness.com, as a tool to promote the business community. He noted that the City and the Chamber of Commerce rejected the offer of the site and the City has now started its own business website.
Steven Lusk, Tustin: announced that he is a graduate student at Cal State Fullerton and he is conducting research for his thesis. He is looking for Mission Viejo baby boomers to participate in a survey that will help him understand the impacts of the housing crash on the migration and employment decisions for those residents born between 1946 and 1964. Interested parties can contact him at shark92672@gmail.com .
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: reminded the community that tomorrow is election day and she encouraged residents to get the facts, be courteous to one another, and get out to vote.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 7 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 15, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register Dated October 5, 2012 in the Amount of $3,846,740.71
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated October 12, 2012 in the amount of $944,585.08
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Check Register dated October 19, 2012 in the amount of $1,779,884.39
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
Biennial City Commission Member Term Expiration
(1) Directed the City Clerk to post the Notice of City Commission Vacancies, (2) set application deadline for December 14, 2012, and (3) scheduled appointment of commission members for January 7, 2013.
8.
Jeronimo Road Pavement Resurfacing ( CIP 837)
(1) Authorized issuance of a purchase order for design services for the subject project to Joseph C. Truxaw and Associates, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $48,000, and (2) approved the agreement with the Orange County Transportation Authority for funding under the State-Local Partnership Program.
9.
Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791) - Acquisition of Right-of-Way from Watermarke Properties, Inc.
(1) Approved the Agreement for Acquisition of Real Property between the City of Mission Viejo and Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development LP (Watermarke Properties, Inc.) for the purchase of the necessary right-of-way and easements required for the widening of Oso Parkway from I-5 to Country Club Drive subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney and City Engineer; and (2) authorized the City Clerk to record the easement deeds in the office of the County Recorder subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney and City Engineer.
10.
Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791) - Acquisition of Right-of-Way from Sunrise Assisted Living
(1) Approved the Agreement for Acquisition of Easements between the City of Mission Viejo and SZR Mission Viejo Assisted Living (Sunrise Assisted Living) for the purchase of the necessary right-of-way and easements required for the widening of Oso Parkway from I-5 to Country Club Drive subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney and City Engineer; and (2) authorized the City Clerk to record the easement deeds in the office of the County Recorder subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney and City Engineer.
11.
Safe Routes to School (CIP 211)
Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Mora’s Equipment & Construction, Inc., in the amount of $123,275.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
12.
Community Services Funding Program For Fiscal Year 2012-2013
Kelly Doyle, Director of Recreation and Community Services, presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1) approve the Community Services Commission's funding amounts for Fiscal Year 2012-2013 for the Community Services Funding Program in the amount of $75,000, as discussed in the staff report; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-66 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget for Costs Related to the Community Services Funding Program.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
7.
Annual Routine Landscape Maintenance - Marguerite Parkway Slope Rehabilitation
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon asked Assistant City Manager Rattay to outline their email correspondence on bidding for slope rehabilitation projects.
Mr. Rattay responded that the City does not bid these projects in the form of a capital improvement project however slope renovations are bid-upon by the City’s existing landscape maintenance contractors in order to obtain the best price for plant material and irrigation systems.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) approve the Second Amendment to the existing contract with Spectrum Care Landscape, Inc., to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $156,000.00; (2) approve the Eleventh Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc., to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00; (3) approve Third Amendment to the existing contract with John Deere Landscapes, Inc. to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $15,000; and (4) adopt Resolution 12-65 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget for Costs Related to Marguerite Parkway Slope Rehabilitation.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
13.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he received a letter from OCFA indicating that they have not started an investigation into alleged fraudulent disability claims because they have not received any specific information to warrant an investigation. Mr. Wontrobski questioned that position.
Council Member Kelley presented the OCFA report.
14.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
15.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that there is a meeting of the San Joaquin Hills TCA this week and she will have a report at the next City Council Meeting.
16.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
17.
Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas announced that the Successor Agency Oversight Board Meeting for the month of October was canceled. The November meeting may be canceled as well.
City Manager Wilberg reminded the Council that staff will be traveling to Sacramento in two weeks to meet and confer with State officials and staff will report back with an update at the next City Council meeting.
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Bill Curley emphasized that his announcement does not put the City in peril or jeopardy but provides an update on a matter that came to the Council's attention at the last meeting. Mr. Curley noted that litigation has been filed against the State to unwind a homeowner's obligation to pay a fee or tax if their home is in a high fire hazard severity zone. He reminded the Council that they took action to set up a Special Fire Protection Area in Mission Viejo, therefore any high fire hazard severity zone fees do not apply to residents of this community. Mr. Curley also noted that the letter referenced at the last Council Meeting was for a property outside of the City of Mission Viejo and no Mission Viejo resident should receive such a notice since Mission Viejo is not part of the State Responsibility Area (SRA.) Those who seek further information should visit the City’s website or the Howard Jarvis website. Council Member Kelly clarified that the resident who mentioned this at the last Council meeting has property outside of Mission Viejo and the fee will be levied for that property.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
18.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley reminded residents that the City of Mission Viejo adopted a Healthy Eating Active Living (HEAL) resolution and one of the cornerstones of that program is the City's weekly Farmers Market. The market is held Fridays from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. in the civic center parking lot and she encouraged residents to come by for fresh, locally grown produce and products. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the Walk Against Drugs on October 20. She stated that it was a wonderfully successful event with several thousand children and families participating. It was another great job by the City's Crime Prevention Specialist, Tammy Descoteaux, the Police Services Department and City staff. She also enjoyed Hometown Halloween and she discussed her attendance, with Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, at the Marine Corps Ball last evening. Council Member Kelley acknowledged the work of Chairman Bruce Hunt and the Marine Adoption Committee which raised $50,000 for the ball. She reminded residents that the City will hold its annual Veterans Day ceremony on November 11 at 2:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center and she congratulated the 2012 male and female Veterans of the Year who will be honored at the ceremony, Bruce Hunt and Valorie Lephart. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of November is thankfulness.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness announced that he recently visited Newhart Middle School and he was impressed by the remodel that has been completed on the campus. He also enjoyed the Walk Against Drugs and the Mayor’s Campout event. 450 residents signed up to attend but unfortunately it rained that day so there were 200 cancelations. He noted that it was still a great event and he thanked staff for doing an outstanding job planning all of the activities.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht stated that it has been an active month with her campaign and City duties. She enjoyed the Walk Against Drugs and Hometown Halloween and she noted that this is a great City that does a lot for its residents. She also announced that prior to the City’s Veterans Day ceremony on November 11, the American Legion will hold its annual pancake breakfast and cruise from 7:00 a.m. to 11 a.m. at the Community Center. Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that tomorrow is a very important day and being a voter is being an activist. She concluded her comments with a quote from Mark Twain: "Each man must for himself alone decide what is right and what is wrong, which course is patriotic and which isn't. You cannot shirk this and be a man. To decide against your conviction is to be an unqualified and excusable traitor, both to yourself and to your country, let me label you as they may."
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon noted that she recently visited Trabuco Canyon Elementary School and she was surprised at how many Mission Viejo children attend the school. She talked with the students about the job of a City Council Member and she enjoyed the experience very much. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon commended Don Snyder, Principal of Del Lago Elementary School, for handling a recent trespassing incident on the campus and for protecting the children. She also stated that she is mindful of the people whose homes were destroyed and the lives that were lost in the wake of hurricane Sandy. She noted that a City employee has family members who live on Staten Island and there was significant damage to their homes. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that CUSD will screen Behind the Orange Curtain on Wednesday, November 7, 2012, at 7:00 p.m. at San Juan Hills High School. The City of Huntington Beach has also screened the film three times so word is getting out and Mission Viejo will continue to work to be part of the solution to a very big problem. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon discussed Cade Spinello's recent visit to City Hall for a school project. Cade interviewed City Manager Wilberg, Lt. Wilson and other members of staff. Cade is a NEGU (Never Ever Give Up) Ambassador and she shared a YouTube video of his recent visit to a UCLA football team practice. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon concluded her comments by thanking Mayor Ury and Council Member Schlicht for keeping things professional and respectful during their campaigns for re-election to the City Council.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury thanked Mayor Pro Tem Reardon for putting things into perspective with the video of young Cade Spinello. He outlined his attendance at the recent Campout with the Mayor, the Walk Against Drugs, and Hometown Halloween. Lastly, Mayor Ury reminded residents to get out and vote tomorrow.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, November 19, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of November 19, 2012
